panels.title: Bytes by Category over Time
panels.description: Stacked bytes per interval by nDPI category. Values are bytes per interval, not a rate. One category often dominates — deselect it in the Category picker to see the tail.

panels.title: Category Share
panels.description: Share of bytes across the currently selected categories.

panels.title: Category Summary
panels.description: Bytes, packets, distinct source hosts and flow-record count per category. '% of all traffic' is measured against every category in the range, not just the selected ones, so the figures stay absolute when you deselect a dominant category. 'Flow records' counts fragments, not sessions: idle_timeout=2 / active_timeout=5 in collector/main.py splits long transfers across many records.

targets.query:
import "array"
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

sel = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
    |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and (r._field == "bytes" or r._field == "packets"))
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.category =~ /^${category:regex}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["category", "_field"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["category"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")

allBytes = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
    |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

total = (union(tables: [allBytes, array.from(rows: [{_value: 0}])])
  |> sum()
  |> findRecord(fn: (key) => true, idx: 0))._value

sel
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with pct: float(v: r.bytes) / float(v: total) * 100.0}))

targets.query:
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Turn the CIDR filter box into an anchored prefix regex. Kept as a regex because that
// is the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage; mask arithmetic per record
// times out on a busy mirror. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32
// round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the range can be wider than
// typed (/20 behaves as /16) -- it never hides matching traffic.
// The split sits in the else branch on purpose: an empty box has no octets to
// index, and Flux evaluates a block's statements eagerly.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

// An empty box means no filtering.
cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

zone = (ip) =>
  if strings.containsStr(v: ip, substr: ":") then "IPv6"
  else if ip == "0.0.0.0" then "0.0.0.0 unspecified"
  else if ip =~ /^10\.10\./ then " 10.10/16"
  else if ip =~ /^(22[4-9]|23[0-9])\./ then "Multicast"
  else if ip =~ /^255\./ or ip =~ /\.255$/ then "Broadcast"
  else if ip =~ /^169\.254\./ then "Link-local"
  else if ip =~ /^127\./ then "Loopback"
  else if ip =~ /^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)/
    then regexp.replaceAllString(r: /\.[0-9]+$/, v: ip, t: ".0/24")
  else "Public"

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.category =~ /^${category:regex}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "category"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({src_zone: zone(ip: r.src_ip), category: r.category, _value: r._value}))
  |> group(columns: ["src_zone", "category"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["src_zone"], columnKey: ["category"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["src_zone"])

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict every panel to traffic with either endpoint in this range, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16, 10.12.6.0/24, or a bare IP. Leave empty for no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary, so /20 behaves as /16 and may show a wider range than typed.

list.name: category
list.label: Category
list.description: nDPI application categories present in the selected time range.
